title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 216 (Investigation of ownership of company)

content.overview: Section 216 empowers the Central Government to appoint one or more inspectors to investigate and report on the membership of any company and other matters relating to the company for the purpose of determining the true persons who are or have been financially interested in the success or failure of the company or who are or have been able to control or materially influence the policy of the company. The section looks through nominees to the persons financially interested. It connects with the significant beneficial owner regime in section 90. It is not an affairs investigation under section 210.
content.glance: CG may appoint inspectors to investigate membership and identify true persons financially interested or able to control/influence policy; looks through nominees; linked to s. 90 SBO; distinct from s. 210 affairs investigation.
content.study: Where it appears to the Central Government that there is good reason to do so, it may appoint one or more inspectors to investigate and report on the membership of any company and other matters relating to the company for the purpose of determining the true persons—(a) who are or have been financially interested in the success or failure, whether real or apparent, of the company; or (b) who are or have been able to control or materially influence the policy of the company. Current-law framing: identify CG appointment for ownership investigation; focus on membership and true controllers/financially interested persons; distinguish from full affairs investigation under s. 210; cross-refer s. 90 significant beneficial ownership.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Determine true persons financially interested in success/failure or able to control or materially influence policy.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: Investigation of membership and related matters; looks through nominees.

sections.heading: Appointment
sections.body: Central Government may appoint one or more inspectors where there is good reason.

sections.heading: Relationship
sections.body: Connects with s. 90 SBO; distinct from s. 210 affairs investigation.

examples.title: Nominee veil
examples.body: Shares are held in the names of nominees. CG appoints an inspector under s. 216 to identify the true persons financially interested and able to control policy.

examples.title: Not a full affairs probe
examples.body: An ownership investigation under s. 216 is ordered. That does not by itself open a full investigation into the company’s affairs under s. 210; the two powers are distinct.

hypotheticals.question: Is s. 216 the same as investigating significant beneficial owners under s. 90?
hypotheticals.analysis: They are related but not the same. Section 90 imposes disclosure duties on significant beneficial owners. Section 216 is the Central Government’s power to appoint inspectors to investigate membership and true controllers. Both address beneficial control from different angles.

distinctions.title: Ownership investigation (s. 216) vs affairs investigation (s. 210)
distinctions.left: Membership and true controllers/financially interested persons
distinctions.right: Investigation into the affairs of the company generally

misconceptions.trap: Section 216 is only about the register of members on the company’s books.
misconceptions.correction: Section 216 is aimed at determining the true persons financially interested or able to control policy, including through nominees — not merely formal register entries.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 216 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm CG appointment for ownership probe. II. Focus on true controllers/financial interest. III. Distinguish s. 210 affairs investigation. IV. Link s. 90 if relevant. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Ownership facts; appointment; true-person findings sought; precise relief.

examTips: True persons financially interested or controlling policy.
